items.title: Modules over a finite simple algebra
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors

items.difficulty_reason: The lemma collects the structure of modules over a finite simple algebra: a unique simple module, finite modules as direct sums of copies of it, isomorphism detected by dimension, the explicit matrix description with its endomorphism skew field, the identification of the algebra with the endomorphisms of the simple module together with the dimension formula, and the matrix-algebra description of the endomorphism algebra of any finite module with its double commutant (statement lines 497-515). The proof is a complete argument: the structure theorem and the equivalence of module categories reduce everything to modules over a skew field, where freeness gives the first three statements (proof lines 517-524); the explicit description of the simple module is transported through the equivalence to obtain the endomorphism statements and the dimension formula (proof lines 525-532); and the last statement follows because a finite module is a direct sum of copies of a simple one (proof lines 533-534). The non-formal content is the transport of the module-theoretic statements through the equivalence. The claim is H2.
